1.title: Read a local property market
1.intro: Property is local. Learn one neighbourhood deeply.
pts: Collect 20 recent sales: price, size, days on market, condition.
Compute price per square foot and the spread.
Note rent levels, vacancy and new supply.
1.ex: 20 sales: median 640 per sq ft; range 560 to 760; median 28 days on market.
1.act: Build a 20-sale table and market note.

2.title: Know licensing, disclosure and trust rules
pts: Provincial regulators license agents and brokers; only licensed people may trade for others.
Deposits go into trust accounts with strict records.
Sellers and agents must disclose known material facts.
2.ex: Row: 'Accept a buyer deposit | provincial real-estate regulator | trust account and receipt | same day | trust ledger'.
2.act: Build a rules table for your province.

3.title: Value and analyse a property
pts: Comparable sales method: adjust for size, condition, location.
Income method: net operating income / capitalisation rate.
Check hidden costs: repairs, taxes, fees.

4.title: Cost a deal and test it
4.ex: Buy 360,000; costs 24,000; sell 420,000; fees 21,000; profit 15,000 (3.5%). A 5% price fall turns it negative. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Build a deal sheet with a 5% fall case.

5.title: Run the transaction and file records
pts: Handle conflicts of interest in writing.
5.ex: Closing checklist with 14 steps, each signed and dated.

7.title: Manage legal, fair-housing and market risk
pts: Fair-housing and human-rights rules forbid discrimination.
Keep records for the required years.
7.ex: Risk: 'Price fall | 4 x 4 | margin of safety | owner | quarterly'.

8.title: Pilot with a paper deal
pts: Pick a listing, value it and plan the sale.
Stop rule: negative margin means no deal.
8.act: Run the mock and present review.
